---
title: "Work inside a nest"
description: "Open a nest to edit its clips in place, find your way back out, and see what stays project-wide while you're inside."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Open a [nest](/editing/nests/) to change the clips inside it without taking the group apart. The nest clip keeps its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, which [Un-nest](/editing/nests/) would throw away.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Open Nest', 'Clip ▸ Close Nest']}
  keys={['⌘↓', '⌘↑']}
  where={['Double-click a nest clip', 'The breadcrumb, in the corner above the track headers']}
  tools="set_scope"
/>

## Open a nest

Double-click a nest clip. You can also select one nest clip and choose **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>).

**Clip ▸ Open Nest** needs exactly one nest clip selected, so it's greyed out with two selected. A double-click doesn't mind what else is selected, because it names its own clip.

A nest can hold nests. Open one the same way from inside, down to eight levels.

Because a double-click opens a nest clip, it can't rename one. Use **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) or the name field in the Clip tab.

## Come back out

Choose **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>), or click the [breadcrumb](#use-the-breadcrumb). Either one goes out one level, and the nest clip you went in through is selected again.

**Clip ▸ Close Nest** is greyed out at the top level. **Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are both greyed out while you're typing in a field, so <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> stay with the text.

## Use the breadcrumb

While a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as `Timeline › Intro`, with a back arrow in front of it.

- It shows the last two levels: the one you'd return to, then the one you're in, in bold. Hover over it for the full path.
- A level is named after the nest clip you went in through, so renaming that clip changes the path.
- A long name is shortened in the middle, so `Lower Third 1` and `Lower Third 2` still look different.

Click anywhere in the corner to go out one level, the same as <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. A double-click counts as one click, so to go up two levels, click twice with a pause or press <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> twice.

With no nest open, the corner is empty and does nothing.

## What you see inside

The timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips, counted from the nest's own zero. That's all of its contents, including anything the nest clip's [trim](/editing/nest-copies/#trim-a-nest-clip) is hiding on the outer timeline.

The canvas shows the nest at its fixed size, without the nest clip's position, scale, opacity or fades, and you hear it without the nest clip's volume. You're editing the group on its own terms, and the nest clip's settings come back when you leave.

## Where the playhead goes

The playhead moves with you, so the frame under it doesn't change. It also carries back out. If a nest clip starts at 10 s and the playhead is at 12 s, you go in at 2 s. Move to 3 s, come out, and you're at 13 s.

That holds while the playhead is over the nest clip. If it's before the clip when you double-click, you go in at the nest's first frame and come out at the clip's start. If it's past the clip's end, or you move past that point inside, the playhead sits on time the nest clip doesn't play, and the canvas inside shows a frame the timeline won't.

Going in or out also stops playback.

## Going in and out isn't an edit

Opening or closing a nest makes no undo step and doesn't mark the project as changed.

- **Selection:** going in clears the selection. Coming out selects the nest clip again.
- **In/out range:** it's cleared both ways, because a range means one thing inside a nest and another on the timeline. You can set a new [range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside, and it loops and ripple deletes in the nest's own time.
- **Reopening:** a project always opens on its timeline, even if you saved with a nest open.

## Edit inside a nest

Every clip edit works inside a nest, in the nest's own times. That includes **Clip ▸ Nest**, which makes a nest inside this one, and **Clip ▸ Un-nest**.

Each edit is one step on the project's single undo history:

- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> after you've come out still undoes an edit you made inside.
- If an undo removes the nest you're in, you land in the deepest level that's left, and the in/out range clears.

When more than one clip shows this nest, your edit reaches all of them. See [Shared copies](/editing/nest-copies/#shared-copies).

The nest clip on the outer timeline keeps its length whatever you do inside. Material you add past its end stays hidden until you drag the clip's end out, and if the contents get shorter, the clip shows nothing over what's left of it.

## What stays project-wide

Some things belong to the project, not to the nest you have open. They still work, and they change the whole project.

- **Media:** the Media tab lists the project's media. Adding, relinking or removing a file works as usual. Dropping a file from Finder onto a nest's timeline adds it to the project and puts its clip in the nest, as one undo step.
- **The Document tab:** it shows the project's settings. Changing the project's size doesn't change the nest's size, which is [fixed](/editing/nests/).
- **Markers:** the Document tab's list stays, but the ruler shows none. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
- **Export:** **File ▸ Export…** writes the whole timeline, not the nest. A range you set inside a nest can't be used, so the **Range** pop-up stays on **Whole project**. Close the nest and set the range on the timeline.

**File ▸ Save Frame…** is the exception: it saves what the canvas shows, so with a nest open you get a frame of the nest.

## What's off while a nest is open

| Command | With a nest open |
| --- | --- |
| **Mark ▸ Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker** | Off, and <kbd>M</kbd> beeps. **Go** in the Document tab's Markers list is disabled too, because a marker is at project time and the playhead inside a nest isn't. |
| **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** | Off. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) only works on the timeline, never inside a nest. |
| **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject** | Off, and the Picture tab has no **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/). |
| **File ▸ New Project from Range…** | Off. See [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/). |
| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | Off. |
| **File ▸ Rename Graphic…** | Off. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/). |
| **Track ▸ Mix…** | **Compressor** and **Limit peaks** are disabled, because a nest's mix plays through the track that holds the nest clip. The track's volume and pan still work. |

## Limits count the whole project

A project holds up to 4,096 clips and 64 tracks, and nests go eight levels deep. Clips and tracks are counted across the timeline and every nest together, and the depth is counted from the timeline. An edit that looks fine inside a nest can still be turned down when the whole project would go over. Frame Job shows an alert with the limit and changes nothing.

A nest's contents count once, however many clips show it. Un-nest the last clip showing a nest to take its tracks out of the count. Deleting that clip leaves them counted.

## With an agent

An agent can open a nest in the window with `set_scope`, as you would. Given a nest two clips show, it goes in through the earlier one. It can also edit inside any nest without opening it. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

## Related

- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)
- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)

A nest clip is a view of a [nest](/editing/nests/), not the nest itself. Two clips can show one nest, so an edit inside it reaches both. This page covers which copies share their contents, how to get one that doesn't, and what a trim does to a nest clip.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Duplicate', 'Clip ▸ Split', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest', 'Clip ▸ Nest']}
  keys={['⌘D', '⌘T', '⇧⌘G', '⌘G']}
  where="⌥-drag a nest clip"
  tools={['duplicate', 'split', 'paste', 'unnest', 'nest']}
/>

## Shared copies

These all leave you with clips that show one nest:

| Do this | You get |
| --- | --- |
| **Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>) | A second clip showing the same nest, straight after the selection. |
| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag a nest clip | A second clip showing the same nest, where you drop it. |
| **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>) | Two clips showing the same nest, cut at the playhead. |

[Open](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest) any of them and edit, and every clip showing that nest changes.

Only the contents are shared. Each nest clip keeps its own place on the timeline, its own length, and its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume.

[Un-nesting](/editing/nests/) one clip gives you its contents as ordinary clips and leaves the others showing the nest. The nest goes when you un-nest the last clip that shows it.

:::caution[A split nest clip starts again]
A nest clip always plays from the nest's first frame. So when you split one, the second part starts from the top of the nest, not from where you cut, and the join shows. The same goes for anything else that cuts through a nest clip, such as a ripple delete over a range.

To cut the contents at a moment, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and split inside it.
:::

## Make an independent copy

To get a copy you can edit on its own, turn a duplicate back into clips and nest them again.

<Steps>

1. Select the nest clip and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. The selection stays on the original.

2. Click the new copy, then press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it. Its contents come out as ordinary clips, all selected.

3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>. Those clips become a new nest, which shares nothing with the first.

</Steps>

Un-nesting drops the copy's own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, so set those again on the new nest clip. The new nest also takes the project's current size, which may differ from the original's. Un-nesting gives back everything in the nest, so a [trim](#trim-a-nest-clip) on the copy is gone too.

:::caution[Copy and Paste don't work on a nest clip]
**Edit ▸ Copy** leaves the nest itself behind, so **Edit ▸ Paste** shows an alert saying the pasted clip shows a nest "which the payload does not carry", and pastes nothing. That's true of any selection with a nest clip in it, in this project or another one.

**Edit ▸ Cut** is worse, because it still removes the clip. Press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> to bring it back.
:::

## Trim a nest clip

Trimming a nest clip changes how much of the nest plays. It never cuts anything out of the nest. The clip always plays from the nest's first frame for as long as the clip lasts, which makes its two edges behave differently from a media clip's:

| Drag | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| The end edge in | The tail of the nest is hidden. |
| The end edge out | More of the nest plays. Past the end of the contents, the clip shows nothing. The contents set no limit on how far you can drag. |
| The start edge later | The clip starts later and the whole nest moves later with it. The opening still plays, and the tail is what gets hidden. |
| The start edge earlier | The nest moves earlier with it, and more of the tail plays. |

So you can't hide a nest's opening with a trim. To do that, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it, which changes every clip showing the nest.

**Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>) gives back everything, however short the clip was trimmed. What was hidden returns at the nest clip's start plus its own time, and a clip that would then collide with what's after it goes on a new track in front.

## With an agent

An agent can make the independent copy in one step. `paste` copies a nest when its payload carries the nest as well as the clip, with every level inside it, and gives the copy nothing in common with the original. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)

---
title: "Work inside a nest"
description: "Open a nest to edit its clips in place, find your way back out, and see what stays project-wide while you're inside."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Open a [nest](/editing/nests/) to change the clips inside it without taking the group apart. The nest clip keeps its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, which [Un-nest](/editing/nests/) would throw away.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Open Nest', 'Clip ▸ Close Nest']}
  keys={['⌘↓', '⌘↑']}
  where={['Double-click a nest clip', 'The breadcrumb, in the corner above the track headers']}
  tools="set_scope"
/>

## Open a nest

Double-click a nest clip. You can also select one nest clip and choose **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>).

**Clip ▸ Open Nest** needs exactly one nest clip selected, so it's greyed out with two selected. A double-click doesn't mind what else is selected, because it names its own clip.

A nest can hold nests. Open one the same way from inside, down to eight levels.

Because a double-click opens a nest clip, it can't rename one. Use **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) or the name field in the Clip tab.

## Come back out

Choose **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>), or click the [breadcrumb](#use-the-breadcrumb). Either one goes out one level, and the nest clip you went in through is selected again.

**Clip ▸ Close Nest** is greyed out at the top level. **Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are both greyed out while you're typing in a field, so <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> stay with the text.

## Use the breadcrumb

While a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as `Timeline › Intro`, with a back arrow in front of it.

- It shows the last two levels: the one you'd return to, then the one you're in, in bold. Hover over it for the full path.
- A level is named after the nest clip you went in through, so renaming that clip changes the path.
- A long name is shortened in the middle, so `Lower Third 1` and `Lower Third 2` still look different.

Click anywhere in the corner to go out one level, the same as <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. A double-click counts as one click, so to go up two levels, click twice with a pause or press <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> twice.

With no nest open, the corner is empty and does nothing.

## What you see inside

The timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips, counted from the nest's own zero. That's all of its contents, including anything the nest clip's [trim](/editing/nest-copies/#trim-a-nest-clip) is hiding on the outer timeline.

The canvas shows the nest at its fixed size, without the nest clip's position, scale, opacity or fades, and you hear it without the nest clip's volume. You're editing the group on its own terms, and the nest clip's settings come back when you leave.

## Where the playhead goes

The playhead moves with you, so the frame under it doesn't change. It also carries back out. If a nest clip starts at 10 s and the playhead is at 12 s, you go in at 2 s. Move to 3 s, come out, and you're at 13 s.

That holds while the playhead is over the nest clip. If it's before the clip when you double-click, you go in at the nest's first frame and come out at the clip's start. If it's past the clip's end, or you move past that point inside, the playhead sits on time the nest clip doesn't play, and the canvas inside shows a frame the timeline won't.

Going in or out also stops playback.

## Going in and out isn't an edit

Opening or closing a nest makes no undo step and doesn't mark the project as changed.

- **Selection:** going in clears the selection. Coming out selects the nest clip again.
- **In/out range:** it's cleared both ways, because a range means one thing inside a nest and another on the timeline. You can set a new [range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside, and it loops and ripple deletes in the nest's own time.
- **Reopening:** a project always opens on its timeline, even if you saved with a nest open.

## Edit inside a nest

Every clip edit works inside a nest, in the nest's own times. That includes **Clip ▸ Nest**, which makes a nest inside this one, and **Clip ▸ Un-nest**.

Each edit is one step on the project's single undo history:

- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> after you've come out still undoes an edit you made inside.
- If an undo removes the nest you're in, you land in the deepest level that's left, and the in/out range clears.

When more than one clip shows this nest, your edit reaches all of them. See [Shared copies](/editing/nest-copies/#shared-copies).

The nest clip on the outer timeline keeps its length whatever you do inside. Material you add past its end stays hidden until you drag the clip's end out, and if the contents get shorter, the clip shows nothing over what's left of it.

## What stays project-wide

Some things belong to the project, not to the nest you have open. They still work, and they change the whole project.

- **Media:** the Media tab lists the project's media. Adding, relinking or removing a file works as usual. Dropping a file from Finder onto a nest's timeline adds it to the project and puts its clip in the nest, as one undo step.
- **The Document tab:** it shows the project's settings. Changing the project's size doesn't change the nest's size, which is [fixed](/editing/nests/).
- **Markers:** the Document tab's list stays, but the ruler shows none. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
- **Export:** **File ▸ Export…** writes the whole timeline, not the nest. A range you set inside a nest can't be used, so the **Range** pop-up stays on **Whole project**. Close the nest and set the range on the timeline.

**File ▸ Save Frame…** is the exception: it saves what the canvas shows, so with a nest open you get a frame of the nest.

## What's off while a nest is open

| Command | With a nest open |
| --- | --- |
| **Mark ▸ Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker** | Off, and <kbd>M</kbd> beeps. **Go** in the Document tab's Markers list is disabled too, because a marker is at project time and the playhead inside a nest isn't. |
| **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** | Off. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) only works on the timeline, never inside a nest. |
| **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject** | Off, and the Picture tab has no **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/). |
| **File ▸ New Project from Range…** | Off. See [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/). |
| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | Off. |
| **File ▸ Rename Graphic…** | Off. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/). |
| **Track ▸ Mix…** | **Compressor** and **Limit peaks** are disabled, because a nest's mix plays through the track that holds the nest clip. The track's volume and pan still work. |

## Limits count the whole project

A project holds up to 4,096 clips and 64 tracks, and nests go eight levels deep. Clips and tracks are counted across the timeline and every nest together, and the depth is counted from the timeline. An edit that looks fine inside a nest can still be turned down when the whole project would go over. Frame Job shows an alert with the limit and changes nothing.

A nest's contents count once, however many clips show it. Un-nest the last clip showing a nest to take its tracks out of the count. Deleting that clip leaves them counted.

## With an agent

An agent can open a nest in the window with `set_scope`, as you would. Given a nest two clips show, it goes in through the earlier one. It can also edit inside any nest without opening it. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

## Related

- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)
- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)

not_covered.reason: Documented, but not as briefed. The brief, docs/guide/editing.md and features.json all say Copy and Paste make an independent copy of a nest, and by the code they don't. clipboardPayload in app/Sources/EditorViewController+Clipboard.swift returns only clips and media, and no Swift file writes a nests key. Core paste (reachable_nests in core/src/edit_paste.rs) then errors with 'a pasted clip shows nest N, which the payload does not carry', and the app shows that as an alert with nothing pasted. Cut still deletes the clip first. This comes from reading the code; I did not run it in the app, because Copy would overwrite the owner's clipboard. The page therefore gives a route that works (Duplicate, Un-nest the copy, Nest again), a caution about Copy, Paste and Cut, and an agent route through paste. The heading is 'Make an independent copy'.

input.notes:
Both pages pass check-pages.mjs and docs_site_proof.py --pages with 0 problems. I did not run a site build, as instructed. Anchors are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kevingalligan-devel-framejob/9cfd7405-83ec-4caa-905f-7b97a20f2cc9/scratchpad/inventory/anchors/editing-4.json, all 12 features. The anchors differ from the brief's anchor values, so features.json needs remapping from that file.

Needs a decision from the owner: Copy and Paste of a nest clip looks like a real app bug, because the module doc of core/src/edit_paste.rs says the pasteboard carries 'any nest they show'. I did not file an issue. If the app is fixed, the caution on editing/nest-copies needs replacing. Until then, features.json's summary for editing-independent-nest-copies is wrong, and so are docs/guide/editing.md and possibly the pages for editing/nests, editing/copy-and-paste and mcp/tools-copy-and-nest. The paste tool's catalog text also names only clips and media as the payload, while the core accepts nests too. The nest-copies page says an agent can paste with nests in the payload, based on reading the core and the handler. tools-copy-and-nest should agree with that.

Other places where the code differs from the brief or guide, written as the code has it:
- Trimming a nest clip's start edge doesn't hide the opening. The whole nest moves later and the tail is what gets hidden.
- Splitting a nest clip, or a ripple delete through one, makes the second part replay from the nest's first frame.
- 'The nest is only removed once no clip shows it' holds only for Un-nest. Delete leaves the nest in the project, and its clips and tracks still count toward the limits.
- The playhead keeps its frame only while it is over the nest clip.
- More is off inside a nest than the guide lists: Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject and the Behind Subject section, File ▸ New Project from Range…, File ▸ Make Vertical Version…, File ▸ Rename Graphic…, and Compressor and Limit peaks in Track ▸ Mix….

Links to /editing/nests/ point at the page only, since another agent owns it. No Shot on either page, because no capture shows the inside of a nest.
